pr_title: schema sync on columns without precision, width or default (close #2737,#2333)
pr_comments: Yes, it looks like it fixes that issue too.

To summarize what this PR do:
- removed support for `precision: null` as discussed earlier(breaking, so not sure if should be against master or next)
- fixed default values handling in schema sync(`defualt: null` is same as `default: undefined`)
- fixed width property handling on columns set as unsigned
This should be against `next` since we also drop mysql 5.5 (right?). Lets keep this PR open since we should merge master into next first...
Note for the future: changing base branch on PR should be done only after base branch is merged, otherwise we got a lot of mess :)

What's the status of this? What needs to be done?

It's starting to get painful having to ignore junk migrations being generated and not 100% knowing that my database schema is correct.
Implementation is finished. Tests on next were(and still are) failing but it doesn't seem related to this PR.
Other PRs seem to have successful builds, perhaps try merging base (next) into the branch and push. That may trigger a successful build.

To make it work we would need 'green' next branch. Since merging master with next branch have test which are failing, so rebase on any of those commits will also result in failing build. We can't use older next version, because changes are required in CockroachDriver which is new.
However there are 2 PRs open which will fix current tests, so it shouldn't be long now.

Looking forward to this release, removing redundant migration inserts/deletes/alters are getting annoying.

You guys are all doing a fantastic job - trying to convince my company to donate to typeorm 👍
@Kononnable Which PRs are the 2 PRs that are needed to fix the tests?

Sorry guys, it should have been merged long time ago.
Only one unrelated sqlite test and most of cockroachdb tests are failing, so looks ok to merge.

I guess I should check participating notification more often when I'm not checking all notifications for some time.

issue_context.title: MySQLDriver findChangedColumns (fields: width, precision)
issue_context.body:
**Issue type:**

[ ] question
[x] bug report
[ ] feature request
[ ] documentation issue

**Database system/driver:**

[ ] `cordova`
[ ] `mongodb`
[ ] `mssql`
[x] `mysql` / `mariadb`
[ ] `oracle`
[ ] `postgres`
[ ] `sqlite`
[ ] `sqljs`
[ ] `react-native`
[ ] `expo`

**TypeORM version:**

[ ] `latest`
[ ] `@next`
[x] `0.2.7` (or put your version here)

**Steps to reproduce or a small repository showing the problem:**

MySQL version: 5.7
Typescript version: 3.0.1

Everytime schema:sync is called, typeorm drops all fk and re-create them. It also performs alter table change column to timestamp columns. The problem is when findChangedColumns is called.
[Line](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/a4dec02cc59d3219a29c7be0322af2253e1452dc/src/driver/mysql/MysqlDriver.ts#L623)

```ts
console.log("width:", tableColumn.width, columnMetadata.width);
console.log("precision:", tableColumn.precision, columnMetadata.precision);
```

output:

for fk:
```ts
width: 10 undefined
```

for timestamp:
```ts
precision: 0 null
```

Example entity:

```ts
@Entity('assignments')
export class Assignment {

  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn({unsigned: true})
  id: number;

  @CreateDateColumn({precision: null, type: 'timestamp', default: () => 'CURRENT_TIMESTAMP'})
  from: Date;

  @Column({precision: null, type: 'timestamp', default: () => null, nullable: true})
  to: Date;
```
comments:
It my case the comparison of default values fails because of case difference. The `MysqlDriver#compareDefaultValues` ends up comparing the following values:

```javascript
"CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6)" === "current_timestamp(6)"
```

Running:

- `typeorm@0.2.19` (`@latest`)
- `mariadb  5.5.5-10.3.13-MariaDB-1:10.3.13+maria~bionic mariadb.org binary distribution`
   docker image: `mariadb:10`
   sha256: `e93652b8b80d422415a7771c0cd281d4b9922e1fcbc7f775cf5d3b162b8dc81d`) 
   command: `['mysqld', '--character-set-server=utf8mb4', '--collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci']`

I've also tested this on `mariadb:latest`.

Notice the case difference of the default value in `mysql` CLI utility when executing `CREATE TABLE` and `SHOW CREATE TABLE`:

```mysql
mysql> CREATE TABLE test(created_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6));
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.02 sec)

mysql> SHOW CREATE TABLE test;
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table | Create Table                                                                                                                                               |
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| test  | CREATE TABLE `test` (
  `created_at` timestamp(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(6)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci |
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

The `MysqlDriver#mappedDataTypes.createDateDefault` and `MysqlDriver#mappedDataTypes.updateDateDefault` are both set to `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6)`.

I'm not sure if all versions of MariaDB and/or MySQL behave the same, but I guess the comparison here should be case-insensitive.

---
### Update 

I tried to test this on `mysql:latest`, and it looks like the issue here is non-existent:

```mysql
Server version: 8.0.17 MySQL Community Server - GPL

mysql> create database test;
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.02 sec)

mysql> use test;
Database changed
mysql> CREATE TABLE test(created_at TIMESTAMP(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6));
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.03 sec)

mysql> SHOW CREATE TABLE test;
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table | Create Table                                                                                                                                               |
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| test  | CREATE TABLE `test` (
  `created_at` timestamp(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(6)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci |
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

**Edit** A workaround seems to be to explicitly set the default values of `createDate` and `updateDate` columns to `current_timestamp(6)`, but then it gets tricky to use the same base entity config with different databases.

### Update 2

The unique column indices also get recreated. This is because the following check fails at:

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/13ac22242ad1e2a46cc3aa6af870f4b1cfae1af3/src/driver/mysql/MysqlQueryRunner.ts#L1268

```
dbIndex["NON_UNIQUE"] === "0"
```

The value of `dbIndex["NON_UNIQUE"]` on MariaDB is `0`, but the type is `Number` so this check fails.

**Edit** I just realized this has been happening because the type of `NON_UNIQUE` column in `INFORMATION.SCHEMA` is `BIGINT(1)`, and I had the `bigNumberStrings` option explicitly set to `false`.

### Update 3

I've created a patch for my problem with create date in Mariadb. During that process I've realized that the issue I've described above is not related to the initial issue. I will be opening a new issue  and create a pull request linking to that issue.
